overview: Both change a population's allele frequencies without being driven by fitness, but one is internal chance and the other comes from outside migration.
genZNote: Drift: internal randomness. Gene flow: new characters walking in from another population.

aspects.label: Source of Change
aspects.valueA: Random sampling error within an existing population, generation to generation.
aspects.valueB: Movement of alleles between populations via migration and interbreeding.

aspects.label: Effect on Genetic Diversity
aspects.valueA: Tends to reduce genetic diversity within a population over time.
aspects.valueB: Tends to increase genetic diversity by introducing new alleles, and makes populations more similar to each other.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: A random storm kills a non-representative subset of a beetle population (bottleneck effect).
aspects.valueB: Pollen carried by wind introducing new alleles into a neighbouring plant population.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Gene flow generally opposes speciation by homogenising gene pools, while drift can accelerate it in isolated populations.
overlay.memoryTrick: Drift = internal chance. Flow = alleles flowing in from elsewhere.
overlay.commonMisconception: Gene flow is not the same as natural selection — it doesn't favour any particular allele, it just mixes populations.
